Stated Claim / Post Context:
Cost of Living Approval for Trump Falls to 17% in New AP Poll

Only 17% of Americans approve of Trump's handling of the cost of living in a new AP-NORC poll, as most blame his policies for high prices ahead of the midterms.

Actual Article Body:
Donald Trump

Only 17% of Americans approve of how Donald Trump is handling the cost of living, according to a new poll from The Associated Press and the NORC Center for Public Affairs Research, while 82% disapprove.

The poll surveyed 2,140 adults from September 24 to 28, about five weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. It found Trump’s approval on the economy overall at 26%, the lowest of his second term and a 14 point drop from March 2025, right after he returned to office. His overall job approval sits at 31%, with 69% disapproving.

The frustration runs straight back to his own campaign. Trump ran in 2024 promising to bring prices down after years of high inflation under Joe Biden. Now about 7 in 10 Americans say his handling of the cost of living has been worse than they expected, and that includes 52% of Republicans.

Actual Article Body:
Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on Sunday President Donald Trump believed preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon was worth risking short-term energy price increases before deciding to strike the country in February.

While speaking with Margaret Brennan on Face the Nation, Wright said gas prices would come down in the coming months and declined to comment on whether or not he thinks Trump will resume military action following November’s midterm elections. Wright also offered insight into Trump’s decision-making before he chose to strike Iran last winter, saying the president sacrificed political standing in order to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.
